Every ground-truth line and every quiz key was read out of the fixture. Quiz questions are answered by Jev from the final message ALONE. groundTruth.note: Every figure here was read out of the fixture. A claim the message makes that this does not mention is not a contradiction — only a claim that conflicts with something stated here is. This copy extends the one in tasks.json, which says the waiting count climbs steadily and so made a true observation, the drop at 03:15, read as a contradiction. The lines added here were each read out of the fixture on 2026-09-21.
groundTruth.root_cause: Deploy dep-4471 (service gateway, author a.novak, 02:12:00Z to 02:14:00Z, summary "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation") applied config generation 119, which flipped gateway.pool.perRequest from false to true. Taking a connection per request exhausted the fixed 20-connection pool.
groundTruth.config_change_applied_at: 2026-03-14T02:13:41.234Z. Logged as generation 119 applied, 3 keys changed: "gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true", "gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500", and "gateway.log.sampleRate: 1.0 -> 1.0" which is a no-op change to the same value.
groundTruth.first_failure: 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z, req-07401. Two lines at that timestamp: "ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms" and "ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)". A slow-acquire WARN for req-07400 precedes it at 02:14:14.920Z.
groundTruth.gap_between_config_and_first_failure: The config applied at 02:13:41.234Z and the first 503 is at 02:14:18.972Z, so the gap is 37.7 seconds. Anything in the range of roughly 35 to 40 seconds is correct. Measuring instead from the deploy finishing at 02:14:00Z gives about 19 seconds, which is also defensible if the message says that is what it measured.
groundTruth.impact_window: Starts 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z. Still failing at the last line of the log, 2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z. About one hour and forty-five minutes, and unresolved. The log header says node-3 of 3, so it covers one node.
groundTruth.failed_request_count: Exactly 530 lines match "ERROR access ... 503" and exactly 530 lines match ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED. A count of 530 is correct. A count derived from grepping the string "503" alone gives 548 and is wrong, because it also matches request ids and latencies.
groundTruth.pool_before: Before the change the periodic "INFO pool stats" lines read size=20 with in_use oscillating roughly between 3 and 11, idle making up the rest, and waiting=0 throughout.
groundTruth.pool_after: After the change every stats line reads size=20 in_use=20 idle=0. The waiting count climbs by 20 every five minutes, from 12 at 02:15:58Z to 232 at 03:10:58Z. At 03:15:58Z it reads 12 again, and nothing in the log explains the drop. It then climbs again, reaching 172 at 03:55:58Z. in_use stays at 20 and idle at 0 through the drop, and the 503s continue through it. Individual ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED lines report waiting counts up to 232, and the last one, at 03:59:27.974Z, reports 74. The pool never recovers.
groundTruth.workers: logs/worker.log has 1080 "finished ok" job lines and no ERROR line. All 18 of its pool stats samples read size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0. Job durations rise gradually across the whole log, from 200ms at 01:00 to 2324ms at 03:59, with no step at 02:14. Its only WARN is a 1.9s slow query at 02:36:22Z, tagged known issue OPS-2210.
groundTruth.red_herrings: dep-4468 (catalog-svc, 22:04Z on Mar 13) and dep-4469 (accounts-svc, 23:31Z on Mar 13) are hours early and on other services. dep-4470 (worker, 00:48Z) is over an hour early and the workers never failed. dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41Z) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc, 03:20Z) both ship after the failures already started, so neither can be the cause. The OPS-2210 slow query is a known pre-existing issue.
groundTruth.correct_next_action: Roll back dep-4471, or revert gateway.pool.perRequest to false. Nothing else in the evidence points anywhere useful. No worker action is needed.
groundTruth.config_reload: A config reload was requested by the deploy pipeline at 02:12:12.820Z, generation 118 -> 119, and generation 119 applied at 02:13:41.234Z.
groundTruth.slow_acquire: There are 212 "acquire slow" WARN lines. The first is req-07400 at 02:14:14.920Z, waited 100ms. The last is at 03:59:19.870Z, waited 890ms.
groundTruth.requests_after_first_failure: From the first 503 to the end of the log there are 636 access lines. 530 of them are 503s. The other 106 are /health checks, which keep returning 200 throughout.

groundTruth.failing_tests: Before any change `node run-tests.js` reports 625 total, 622 passing, 3 failing, and exits non-zero. All three failures are in the group named order totals and all call orderTotal: case 433 orderTotal(12000, 15, 0.0825) expected 11042 got 11190, case 434 orderTotal(8650, 20, 0.05), and case 435 orderTotal(33400, 10, 0.2) expected 36072 got 36740. They are the only order-total rows where both the discount and the tax are non-zero, which is why the other rows passed.
groundTruth.root_cause: In src/pricing.js the function orderTotal, which starts at line 39, computes tax at line 41 as roundCents(cents * taxRate), on the full price before the discount. The comment above it says tax is charged on the amount the customer pays, so tax has to be computed on the discounted amount.
groundTruth.correct_fix: Any change that computes the tax on the discounted amount is correct. Two equivalent ways are roundCents(discounted * taxRate) added to the discounted amount, and returning applyTax(discounted, taxRate). They give the same totals. Only orderTotal needs to change, and the tests themselves are correct.
groundTruth.after_fix: With that change the suite reports 625 passing and 0 failing.

groundTruth.entry: src/cli.js accepts one command, report. Any other command prints the usage line `usage: cli.js report` to stderr and returns exit code 1. For report it writes toTable(buildRows()) plus a newline to stdout and returns 0.
groundTruth.build_rows: buildRows in src/report.js reads data/runs.json, maps every run to an object with id, suite, status, ms, owner and slow, where slow is true when ms is over 5000, and sorts the rows by ms from high to low, so the slowest run comes first. Every field a run carries survives this step.
groundTruth.to_table: toTable in src/format.js prints only the columns id, suite, status and ms. It deliberately drops owner and slow, because the table is too narrow for them and the slow runs are already at the top. Each column is padded to its widest value. The output is a header line, a line of dashes, then one line per row.
groundTruth.gotcha: Anything that needs the whole row, such as owner or slow, has to take it from buildRows, not from the table.
groundTruth.data: data/runs.json holds five runs. The slowest is r-105, the billing suite, a fail at 9120 ms, and it is the only run over 5000 ms. Then r-108 at 4400 ms, r-106 at 2310 ms, r-104 at 1840 ms and r-107 at 0 ms.

groundTruth.trigger: logs/crash.txt shows auth.internal answering 400 with {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"refresh token revoked"}, then an unhandled rejection and a 500. The session resume failure rate is 100% over a 30 second window.
groundTruth.where_it_surfaces: The stack trace reads: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split') at decode (src/auth/tokens.js:6) called from resumeSession (src/session.js:8).
groundTruth.real_cause: In src/auth/refresh.js the catch block returns undefined at line 15 when the error code is not in the RECOVERABLE set. RECOVERABLE holds only token_expired and clock_skew. invalid_grant is deliberately left out because a revoked refresh token is not retryable and the user has to sign in again. So refreshToken resolves to undefined instead of throwing.
groundTruth.chain: resumeSession in src/session.js passes that undefined straight to decode, and decode calls split on it, which is where the TypeError appears.
groundTruth.nothing_changed: The request said not to fix anything. No file should have been edited.

groundTruth.first_failure: At 2026-07-04T02:14:07.113Z the api logs "redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379". Traffic before that line is healthy, all 200 responses.
groundTruth.cascade: One millisecond later the api logs "cache layer degraded — falling back to direct store reads". Cache miss storms follow, then "TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)" across api, workers and scheduler. Redis reconnect attempts keep failing with the same ECONNREFUSED.
groundTruth.queue: Request queue depth warnings start at 52 of a maximum of 500 at 02:14:12 and climb past the cap, reaching 568 at 02:31:24.
groundTruth.end: At 02:31:44 worker-2 dies with "JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)" and exits with code 134. At 02:31:52 the supervisor logs "api unresponsive, killing process group — service down". That is the last line of the log.
groundTruth.duration: About seventeen and a half minutes from the Redis failure to the service going down.
